Inter-segmental timing delay (Δt_ij) acts as a scalar parameter governing the phase coherence of limb segments during landing. When Δt_ij exceeds critical thresholds, it disrupts the natural deceleration sequence, forcing compensatory mechanisms that amplify anterior tibial shear and patellar tendon forces. This manifests as a shift from vertical to horizontal landing strategies, where stiffness increases and joint range decreases—resulting in higher kinetic dissipation rates (Ė_diss). Failure modes arise when Δt_ij exceeds adaptive capacity, triggering cascading effects in joint mechanics and increasing injury risk.
